claims.statement: A generic failure signal is insufficient for safe recovery: the runtime that treated every failure alike duplicated effects, retried refusals and made a false claim.

Failure classification distinguishes operationally different conditions: every failure the classified runtime met carried a specific class and a certainty, and no stated certainty was contradicted by the provider.
Execution certainty changes the correct recovery action, and a deterministic matrix chose the preregistered action in every scenario.
Blind retry can duplicate external side effects: in the flagship, the naive runtime credited the customer twice for one request.
Reconciliation resolves ambiguous outcomes: the classified runtime asked the system of record instead of resending and committed one effect, including where an idempotency key could not help.

Checkpoint and resume must preserve operation semantics, not only workflow position: with intent and result records the classified runtime resumed every crash without a duplicate, and a step-only checkpoint (X3) duplicated a credit.
Trace continuity makes multi-attempt execution diagnosable: the classified runtime kept every run in one trace across SIGKILL and resume; a trace held in memory split every crashed run.
Deterministic eval invariants and recovery evals detect reliability regressions: every preregistered mutant of the recovery layer failed a check, including one an outcome check could not see.
Without execution certainty (timeouts treated as failed calls), the same runtime duplicated external effects, and broke cleanly rather than crashing.
Observability and evals serve different purposes, and gates keep a changed model safe: the offline gate blocked a behaviour regression that the runtime's invariants also contained.

claims.qualification: two local 8B-class models on sixteen cases; both blocked by the gate
claims.statement: Reliability is the policy that connects evidence to the next safe action: with real models proposing, no unsafe proposal executed, although neither model passed the release gate and retrieval missed three cases.
The evidence holds together: the deterministic run replays byte for byte, and no planted secret reached telemetry.

claims.rests_on: the design argument in the technical edition §17; the POC shows a deterministic policy works, not that a model-based one fails
claims.statement: Recovery decisions should not be delegated to a model: a policy over facts is testable, reproducible and auditable.

claims.rests_on: out of scope; the scenarios are deterministic, single-run and simulated
claims.statement: Behaviour under load, eventual consistency of status queries, partial batch success, and the real distribution of these faults in production.

With a real model making every decision, the reliability results are unchanged: the same duplicates under the baselines, none under the classified runtime, no unsafe credit, and the preregistered decisions.

contract: Production AI Engineering Proof Contract v1

experiments.claim: Retry-everything duplicates effects wherever a sent write lost its outcome; a stable key removes the duplicates the provider can deduplicate; evidence-driven recovery removes them all in the measured scenarios.
experiments.hypothesis: A2: 0 scenarios with a duplicate. A0: exactly S09 S10 S11 S12 S16 S18 S19 S20 S21 S23. A1: exactly S11 S12 S18 S19 S21.
experiments.invariant: I1 and I2: at most one credit per charge, one open ticket and one message per case
limitations: Simulated providers; one deterministic run per scenario; the scenario set is coverage, not a production distribution.
experiments.question: Which runtime commits an external effect more than once when a write loses its outcome?
experiments.setup: 25 preregistered scenarios × 3 runtimes; effects counted in the simulated providers' ledgers.
experiments.title: Duplicate external effects across 25 injected faults (H1–H3)
experiments.variable: the recovery layer (A0 naive, A1 idempotent retry, A2 classified)

experiments.claim: A lost response after a committed write must not trigger a blind second execution; reconciliation by operation id resolves it.
experiments.hypothesis: A0 commits two credits; A2 commits one and dispatches once.
experiments.invariant: one credit for one duplicate charge
limitations: The idempotent runtime is also correct here because this provider honours keys: S09 alone does not separate A1 from A2.
experiments.question: With the same fault, how many credits does each runtime commit, and does the classified runtime send again?
experiments.setup: S09: the credit provider commits, holds the response past the client timeout and closes the connection.
experiments.title: The flagship: the credit committed, the response was lost (S09)

experiments.claim: Recovery can be decided deterministically from evidence, and the decision can be checked against a frozen oracle.
experiments.hypothesis: 25 of 25 decision sequences equal the oracle; every decision recomputes from the matrix.
limitations: The oracle was written by the same author as the matrix; it checks consistency with the preregistered policy, not that the policy is optimal.
experiments.question: Does the classified runtime choose the preregistered (class, certainty, action) sequence in every scenario?
experiments.setup: experiments/scenarios.toml decisions, frozen before the run; config/recovery-matrix.toml.
experiments.title: Recovery decisions equal the preregistered oracle (H4)

experiments.claim: Caution did not cost completions: the classified runtime completed every scenario the oracle marks completable, escalated only where required, and its answers matched the ledgers.
experiments.hypothesis: A2 completes 21 of 21; escalates exactly S12 S13 S19; 0 false claims. A0 and A1 each make at least one false claim.
limitations: A production workload with more tools lacking keys and status queries would escalate more; escalation cost is a person's time, not measured.
experiments.question: Does evidence-driven recovery give up on recoverable work, escalate when it need not, or tell the user something false?
experiments.setup: Oracle status per scenario; answer claims compared with ledgers and confirmed journal state (I9).
experiments.title: The cost of caution: completion, escalation, truthfulness (H5, H6)

experiments.claim: Trace identity restored from durable state keeps a multi-attempt, multi-process run diagnosable.
experiments.hypothesis: A2: no run split across traces. A0 (trace in memory): every SIGKILLed run split.
limitations: Spans of a killed process that had not ended are lost; continuity rests on the journal and a span link.
experiments.question: Does a run stay one trace across worker processes?
experiments.setup: Real SIGKILLs in S15–S18 (and a fail-stop in S23 under A2).
experiments.title: Trace continuity across retries, SIGKILL and resume (H7)

experiments.claim: Deterministic recovery evals detect reliability regressions, including one an outcome check cannot see.
experiments.hypothesis: 8 of 8 mutants detected; A2 0 eval failures.
experiments.invariant: the suite fails on every mutant
limitations: The mutants were chosen by the author; they show sensitivity to plausible bugs, not completeness.
experiments.question: Does each preregistered mutant of the recovery layer fail at least one eval check, while the unmodified runtime fails none?
experiments.setup: 8 one-line mutants × 25 scenarios, the same eval suite.
experiments.title: Evals detect a broken recovery layer (H8)

experiments.claim: Without execution certainty, the same runtime duplicates external effects.
experiments.hypothesis: X1 duplicates an effect in at least one scenario; every X1 run completes normally.
limitations: Where the provider honours keys the bug is masked, not prevented (S09, S16).
experiments.question: If the safeguard (UNKNOWN → reconcile) is removed, does the invariant it protects break, and does the harness still complete?
experiments.setup: The X1 mutant over all 25 scenarios.
experiments.title: Negative control: reconciliation removed (X1, timeout treated as a failed call)
experiments.variable: certainty rules C6 and C7 return NOT_EXECUTED

experiments.claim: Model behaviour may change; deterministic gates and invariants keep recovery semantics fixed.
experiments.hypothesis: scripted-v1 PASS, scripted-v2 BLOCK; v2 through A2 commits no credit and breaks no invariant.
limitations: A scripted regression; the real-model slice is REL-R9.
experiments.question: Does the offline suite block a deterministic behaviour regression, and does the runtime stay safe if it ships anyway?
experiments.setup: 16 slice cases × 3 seeds per scripted model; S00 through all runtimes with scripted-v2.
experiments.title: A model change: the gate blocks it, the invariants hold (H9)

experiments.claim: Whatever a real model proposes, a proposal that fails validation or authorization does not execute.
experiments.hypothesis: H10 is a measurement (not predicted); H11: 0 unsafe proposals executed.
limitations: Sixteen cases, two 8B-class models: a demonstration of the gate, not a model benchmark.
Three cases cannot be grounded: the frozen retriever misses their document.
experiments.question: How do two local models do on the decision, and does any unsafe proposal get past the runtime's gates?
experiments.setup: qwen3:8b and llama3.1:latest via Ollama, 16 cases × 3 seeds, JSON mode, temperature 0.3; deterministic scoring.
experiments.title: The real-model slice (H10, H11)

experiments.claim: The evidence holds together: exact replay, recomputed facts, no canary in telemetry.
experiments.hypothesis: EXACT replay; no difference; no canary hit; tests pass.
limitations: SHA256SUMS is a checksum list, not a signature.
experiments.question: Does the published run replay, are its facts recomputable, and does its telemetry keep secrets out?
experiments.setup: tools/verify_run.py, tools/proof_facts.py, the I11 canary scan, the POC's pytest.
experiments.title: The evidence itself

experiments.claim: The recovery semantics do not depend on the model: with a real model deciding, the duplicate counts, the decisions and the safety invariants are unchanged.
experiments.hypothesis: Not preregistered (added after the published run, at the author's request); reported as a measurement and an invariant.
experiments.invariant: no duplicate and no unsafe credit under A2; the safety invariants hold
limitations: One model, temperature 0: on these three cases it made the same decisions as the scripted stand-in, so this shows the semantics hold with a real model, not across model behaviours.
Run separately (2026-10-07-live), after the published run.
experiments.question: With a real model making every decision instead of the scripted one, do the reliability results hold?
experiments.setup: python -m recovery.run record-live: every scenario x runtime, qwen3:8b via Ollama (temperature 0, seed 1, JSON mode), llama3.1 as the fallback; answers taped.
experiments.title: Real model end to end: the 25 faults with qwen3:8b deciding

Provider time, advanced to expire idempotency keys (S18)
A scripted model for the fault scenarios, so that the recovery layer is the only variable
